# tallyr

tallyr is an R interface to the [Tally](https://tally.so) form builder
[API](https://developers.tally.so). Authenticate with an API key, list
your forms, and import form submissions as tidy tibbles.

## Installation

You can install the development version of tallyr from GitHub with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("EllaKaye/tallyr")
```

## Authentication

Tally uses personal API keys. Create one at [Tally Settings \> API
keys](https://tally.so/settings/api-keys), then store it in the
`TALLY_API_KEY` environment variable in your `.Renviron` (e.g. via
`usethis::edit_r_environ()`):

``` R
TALLY_API_KEY=tly-xxxx
```

To check your setup, run:

``` r

library(tallyr)
tally_sitrep()
```

or, for a quick check that you’re authenticated:

``` r

tally_whoami()
#> ✔ Authenticated with Tally as Ada Lovelace (ada@example.com)
```

## Multiple accounts

If you work with several Tally accounts, store each account’s key in its
own `TALLY_API_KEY_<NAME>` environment variable:

``` R
TALLY_API_KEY=tly-xxxx
TALLY_API_KEY_WORK=tly-yyyy
TALLY_API_KEY_RLADIES=tly-zzzz
```

[`tally_accounts()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_accounts.md)
lists the accounts with a key available, and
[`tally_use_account()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_accounts.md)
switches between them for the rest of the session:

``` r

tally_accounts()
#> [1] "default" "rladies" "work"

tally_use_account("work")
#> ✔ Using Tally account "work"
tally_forms() # uses the "work" account
```

Every API function also takes an `account` argument for one-off calls
without switching:

``` r

tally_forms(account = "rladies")
```

## Importing form data

List your forms to find the ID of the one you want:

``` r

tally_forms()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   id     name                status    number_of_submissions is_closed …
#> 1 3xLJ5V Conference feedback PUBLISHED                    42 FALSE
#> 2 7bQm2W Workshop signup     DRAFT                         0 FALSE
```

Then import its submissions as a wide tibble, with one row per
submission and one column per question:

``` r

tally_submissions("3xLJ5V")
#> # A tibble: 42 × 5
#>   submission_id submitted_at        is_completed `What's your name?` …
#> 1 nWxyzA        2026-06-01 10:00:00 TRUE         Ada
#> 2 nWxyzB        2026-06-02 11:30:00 TRUE         Grace
#> # …
```

Submissions can be filtered by completion status and date:

``` r

tally_submissions(
  "3xLJ5V",
  filter = "completed",
  start_date = "2026-01-01"
)
```

All functions handle pagination automatically and respect Tally’s rate
limit of 100 requests per minute.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`tally_accounts()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_accounts.md)
  [`tally_use_account()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_accounts.md)
  : Work with multiple Tally accounts
- [`tally_api_key()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_api_key.md)
  : Retrieve your Tally API key
- [`tally_forms()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_forms.md)
  : List your Tally forms
- [`tally_sitrep()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_sitrep.md)
  : Situation report for your Tally setup
- [`tally_submissions()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_submissions.md)
  : Import a form's submissions
- [`tally_whoami()`](https://ellakaye.github.io/tallyr/reference/tally_whoami.md)
  : Check who you are authenticated as on Tally
